examples.before:
.troupe/troupe.yml:
name: demo
agents:
  coder: file:agents/coder.yaml

.troupe/agents/coder.yaml:
model: opus
temperature: 0.2

results.1:
all five arms: exit 0, prints:
coder:
  model: opus # from .troupe/agents/coder.yaml
  temperature: 0.2 # from .troupe/agents/coder.yaml
results.2:
exit 0, prints:
coder:
  model: opus # from .troupe/agents/coder.yaml
  temperature: 0.2 # from .troupe/agents/coder.yaml

results.1: all five arms: exit 2, nothing on stdout, the error names the flag. The wording differs by arm: `troupe: unrecognized arguments: --sources`; `troupe: troupe: unrecognized arguments: --sources` ("troupe:" printed twice); `troupe: unrecognized arguments: --sources (see 'troupe --help')`; `troupe: usage error: unrecognized arguments: --sources`; or a usage line `usage: troupe [-h] COMMAND ...` followed by `troupe: error: unrecognized arguments: --sources`
results.2: exit 2, nothing on stdout; stderr: `usage: troupe [-h] {config} ...` then `troupe: error: unrecognized arguments: --sources`

results.1: all five arms: exit 2 with the same message each arm gave for `get`
results.2: exit 2 with the same message it gave for `get`

examples.input: `config set agents.coder.model sonnet --sources`, then `config get agents.coder.model`

results.1: all five arms: the set exits 2 with the unrecognized-arguments error and writes nothing; the follow-up get prints `opus`
results.2: the set exits 2 with the unrecognized-arguments error and writes nothing; the follow-up get prints `opus`

context.in_practice: The two routes behave the same in practice. `--sources` works only on `show`. On `get`, `history` and `set` it fails with exit 2 and changes nothing. Only the wording of the error differs, both between arms on route 1 and between the routes. One arm on route 1 prints "troupe: troupe:" twice.
context.stakes: Whether `--sources` (the annotation showing which file each value came from) works on `show` only or also on the other config commands, and whether passing it to a command that doesn't support it could silently change your config.
context.tradeoff: Route 1 decided on purpose that only `show` takes `--sources`, citing the contract. Route 2 never considered the question but ended up with the same behavior.

plan_why: Shows that `show --sources` adds `# from <file>` comments, then what `get --sources`, `history --sources` and `set --sources` do: route 1 rejects each one with exit 2 and changes no file, while implementations that never considered the question may accept the flag, ignore it or treat it differently.
